nodes.title: NOTE
nodes.summary:
The partial document outlines the fee structure and related policies for students, including those in the FN/NRI category, at an educational institute. Key points include:

1. Continuation of Fees: Students whose studies extend beyond the specified period will continue to pay fees at their last applicable rate. The institute reserves the right to revise fees at any time.

2. Applicability: The fees mentioned are applicable to students admitted in the 2026-27 session and not to future batches.

3. Additional Fees: Students must pay extra fees for backlog or improvement subjects taken during regular or summer semesters.

4. International Engineering Programme (IEP): Students in this program pay 1.5 times the normal fee for the first two years, with subsequent fees determined by the foreign university.

5. Other Charges: Include Student’s Activity & Welfare Charges, Exam Charges, and Medical & Insurance Charges.

6. FN/NRI Category Fees: Details the admission fee and annual program fees for various programs, with a breakdown of tuition, development, and other charges. Scholarships are available for FN/NRI students at admission.

7. Fee Consistency: FN/NRI fees should not be less than those for Indian students, and the same fee structure applies in subsequent years.

8. IEP Specifics: FN/NRI students in IEP pay as per TIET rates for the first two years, with foreign university rates applicable thereafter. If a student fails to meet requirements or opts out, they continue at TIET with FN/NRI fees.

(III) The fees mentioned above in the following years will be applicable to the students who g et 
admission in the session 2026-27. This will not be applicable to the future batches.  
(IV) The student will have to pay additional per subject  fee for the backlog subjects or subjects 
taken for improvement, if taken during the regular /summer  semesters.  
(V) Students admitted under  International Engineering Programme (IEP)  shall pay first two years at 
the rate of 1.5 times of the normal fee as applicable to normal TIET students in that session and 
for balance two years, the amount of fee shall be as prescribed by the respective foreign 
university for that session.  
(VI) Other Charges include Student’s Activity & Welfare Charges  (Rs. 7500) , Exam Charges  (Rs. 
3000)  and Medical & Insurance Charges  (Rs. 500) .

nodes.title: NOTE
nodes.summary:
The partial document outlines the fee structure and related policies for students, including those in the FN/NRI category, at an educational institute. Key points include:

1. Continuation of Fees: Students whose studies extend beyond the specified period will continue to pay fees at their last applicable rate. The institute reserves the right to revise fees at any time.

2. Specific Fees for 2026-27: The fees mentioned are applicable to students admitted in the 2026-27 session and not to future batches.

3. Additional Fees: Students must pay extra fees for backlog or improvement subjects taken during regular or summer semesters.

4. International Engineering Programme (IEP): Students in the IEP pay 1.5 times the normal fee for the first two years, with subsequent fees determined by the foreign university.

5. Other Charges: Include Student’s Activity & Welfare Charges, Exam Charges, and Medical & Insurance Charges.

6. FN/NRI Category Fees: Details the admission fee and annual program fees for various programs, with a breakdown of tuition, development, and other charges. Scholarships are available for FN/NRI students at admission.

7. IEP for FN/NRI Students: Similar fee structure for the first two years as normal FN/NRI students, with subsequent fees set by the foreign university. If students do not continue with IEP, they revert to paying FN/NRI fees at TIET.

8. Other Charges for FN/NRI: Include Student’s Activity & Welfare Charges, Exam Charges, and Medical & Insurance Charges in USD.

The document states that hostel fees for FN/NRI students are the same as for Indian students and mentions that fees are subject to change due to inflation or tariff revisions. It also highlights that accommodation allocation is determined by the Dean of Student Affairs based on program and year, subject to room availability. Laundry services are provided free of charge for hostel students, and all matters related to hostel functioning are managed by the Dean of Student Affairs. No part payment of fees is allowed.
